source.title: DualBreach: Efficient Dual-Jailbreaking via Target-Driven Initialization and Multi-Target Optimization
source.authors: Xinzhe Huang; Ke-Dong Xiu; Tian-Hang Zheng; Churui Zeng; Wang-Ze Ni; Zhan Qin; Kui Ren; Chun Chen

record.tranche_reason: Evaluates harmful-completion rates for a baseline explicitly described as using COLD-Attack’s suffix strategy, a different method aimed at bypassing aligned-model refusals. It does not test fine-tuning or response-position KL.
record.gate_note: Rows record COLD-Attack results because the paper specifies its suffix strategy and reports harmful-response attack success rates. The paper’s DualBreach method is not a test of compliant prefilling or first-token localization. Other attack methods and guardrail-only ASRG results are not included as rows for V4.
record.test_reason: An attack paper (DualBreach) reporting how often its method and baselines get past Llama-Guard-3 plus an aligned LLM. ASRL counts success only if the guardrail passes the prompt AND the LLM answers harmfully. Guardrail blocking caps it: COLD-Attack's Guard3 bypass rate on advBench is only 5%. So these numbers cannot show whether a suffix or compliant opening defeats the model's own refusal. DualBreach uses a 'Sure' vs 'Sorry' target loss as a tool but never measures it separately. No fine-tuning, KL, localization or deepening is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that DualBreach achieves higher dual-jailbreak success with fewer queries than prior attacks, and that their EGuard ensemble outperforms Llama-Guard-3. They draw no conclusion about token-depth of safety.
record.recipe_differences: The cited fine-tuning and token-depth studies are not reproduced. This paper evaluates prompt attacks, including COLD-Attack’s suffix strategy, rather than fine-tuning or per-token distribution changes.
record.method_sensitivity: Success varies with dataset, target model, query setting, and evaluator; StrongReject results differ between Pythia-14m and GPT-4o.

fits_no_version.finding: Attacks optimized jointly against an input guardrail and an aligned LLM reach high joint success: DualBreach ASRL is 86-98% on Llama-3/GPT-4 with Guard3. Single-target attacks are mostly stopped by the guardrail (COLD advBench ASRL 3-18%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dual-jailbreaking: external guardrails plus alignment can be jointly bypassed by prompts optimized for both.

record.peer_reviewed: Network and Distributed System Security (NDSS) Symposium 2026
record.problems: The evaluation samples 100 prompts per dataset, as stated in the experimental setup. No uncertainty estimates are reported. These are attack-success evaluations, not controlled tests of whether a compliant opening causes the bypass.
record.rows_left_out: Other attack-method results and guardrail-only ASRG measurements in Tables II–IV were left out because they do not report the specified COLD suffix-strategy target harmful-completion result. No rows were omitted for the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: No per-token KL or position analysis.
No isolated measure of prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks on model refusal without a guardrail; all success rates are joint with Guard3.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's labels are dropped. They treated low COLD-Attack ASRL as evidence about suffix attacks defeating refusal, but ASRL requires Guard3 to pass the prompt first, and COLD's Guard3 bypass is 4-5% on advBench and harmBench. All rows are baseline comparators in the authors' method comparison. Several one-shot rows marked 'partial' have values equal to or below the Raw baseline. DualBreach's loss pushes toward 'Sure,...' and away from 'Sorry,...', a V4-style mechanism used as a tool, but its effect on the LLM alone is never reported.

versions.untested_parts: No safety model fine-tuning on harmful examples.
Tests a suffix-strategy attack through harmful-completion rates; does not test compliant prefilling, decoding changes, or whether bypass works by getting past the first response tokens.
No test of what causes safety behaviour to be shallow.
No training to deepen safety or evaluation of whether deepening holds up.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: COLD-Attack suffix strategy on DNA with limited queries, and COLD-Attack on StrongReject when judged by Pythia-14m
reader_labels.reason: The reported harmful-completion attack rates are nonzero and reach 67.0%–70.0% on DNA; StrongReject rates are also nonzero under Pythia-14m (rows T2-08–T2-14, T2-40, T2-42, T2-44). These demonstrate some suffix-attack success, not a general opening-token mechanism.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Other datasets and one-shot settings for COLD-Attack
reader_labels.reason: Success rates vary substantially by dataset and target model, and are often low; on DNA, one-shot rates range from 18.0% to 44.0%, while many advBench and harmBench rates are only 1.0%–11.0% (rows T2-01–T2-07, T2-15–T2-23, T2-25–T2-39).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Claude-3.5 on advBench in one-shot setting; StrongReject results judged by GPT-4o
reader_labels.reason: COLD-Attack records zero ASRL for Claude-3.5 on advBench and zero StrongReject ASR under GPT-4o for all three evaluated target models (rows T2-24, T2-41, T2-43, T2-45).
